security_audit.summary: All 13 static findings are false positives involving Markdown backticks or readable multilingual text, not shell substitution or concealed payloads. No evidence found of prompt injection, exfiltration, network access, or destructive operations. A reproduced Unicode normalization bypass contradicts the stated ASCII-only input policy and is recorded as a low-severity semantic finding.

remediation.issue: National ID normalization can accept non-ASCII letters despite the documented rejection policy.
remediation.suggestion: Reject non-ASCII input before stripping or uppercasing in pid_ok. Add a regression test using U+017F followed by 123456784.

semantic_findings.title: Unicode Normalization Bypasses ASCII-Only Input Policy
semantic_findings.description: Uppercasing before validation converts Unicode U+017F to ASCII S, allowing a non-ASCII identifier through the regex and checksum. This contradicts the documented rejection policy.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: A constructed input containing U+017F followed by 123456784 normalizes to S123456784 and passes the documented regex and checksum. The original input is non-ASCII.

content.user_title: Validate Taiwan Business and ID Checksums
content.value_statement: Mistyped Taiwan identifiers can cause errors in forms and records. This skill provides local checksum calculations and format checks without database access.
actual_capabilities: Check eight-digit Taiwan Unified Business Numbers using weighted digit sums and divisibility by five.
Handle the business-number exception when the seventh digit is seven.
Validate national ID checksums using the letter mapping table and weighted digits.
Accept new-format residence certificate numbers with second digits eight or nine through the documented identifier validator.
Normalize lowercase national ID letters and surrounding whitespace before checking the format.
Provide local Python examples and regression vectors for ordinary, invalid, and special-case inputs.
limitations: Checksum results do not confirm company existence, personal identity, document issuance, or authenticity; no registry lookup is provided.
Old-format residence certificates with a letter in the second position are unsupported.
The supplied examples require Python 3; this skill is guidance, not a packaged validation service.
The ID validator uppercases before checking characters, so some non-ASCII letters can pass despite the documented ASCII-only policy.

use_cases.title: Review Form Validation
use_cases.description: Check business-number and identity-number validation rules before adding them to a Taiwan registration form.

use_cases.title: Check Business Record Quality
use_cases.description: Identify business-number format and checksum errors in authorized records without treating passing results as proof of registration.

use_cases.title: Build Regression Coverage
use_cases.description: Use documented examples to test malformed inputs, changed check digits, and the seventh-digit business-number exception.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Business Number
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the checksum of Taiwan business number 22099131. State whether it passes and clarify that this does not verify company registration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: validate one documented public business number.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an Invalid ID Checksum
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the canonical test values A123456789 and A123456788. Explain the checksum difference without making claims about identity or document authenticity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: understand a changed check digit.

prompt_templates.title: Exercise the Business Number Exception
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why synthetic business number 10000073 requires the seventh-digit exception. Compare its ordinary weighted sum with the alternative contributions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Input Validation Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design tests for both validators covering malformed lengths, lowercase letters, non-ASCII characters, residence certificate formats, and 10000073. Identify normalization-related limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review input boundaries and regression coverage.

output_examples.input: Check the checksum of public business number 22099131.
output_examples.output: Checksum passes. The weighted digit sum is 30, which is divisible by five. This result does not verify company registration.

output_examples.input: Check synthetic business number 10000073 and explain the special case.
output_examples.output: Checksum passes through the seventh-digit exception. The ordinary sum is 14; replacing the seventh-digit contribution with one produces five.

output_examples.input: Compare canonical ID test values A123456789 and A123456788.
output: These results do not establish document issuance or authenticity.

best_practices: Use public business numbers or synthetic test vectors; avoid submitting real personal identifiers when examples are sufficient.
Report format and checksum results separately from registration, issuance, authenticity, or legal conclusions.
Test 10000073 for the seventh-digit exception and reject non-ASCII ID input before normalization when strict ASCII validation is required.
anti_patterns: Treating a passing checksum as proof that a company exists or an identity document is genuine.
Guessing missing digits or silently repairing malformed identifiers to make them pass.
Assuming every digit change fails or using 97176270 alone to test the seventh-digit exception.

faq.question: Does this skill need internet access or an API key?
faq.answer: No. The supplied examples perform local calculations without network calls, API keys, or database access.

faq.question: Which identifiers are supported?
faq.answer: Eight-digit business numbers, national ID numbers, and new-format residence certificate numbers with second digits eight or nine are covered.

faq.question: Does a passing checksum prove that a number was issued?
faq.answer: No. A passing checksum only establishes conformity with the calculation rule, not registration, identity, issuance, or authenticity.

faq.question: Why is synthetic business number 10000073 useful?
faq.answer: It fails the ordinary calculation but passes the seventh-digit exception, making it useful for regression testing.

faq.question: How are lowercase letters and non-ASCII inputs handled?
faq.answer: The ID validator strips whitespace and uppercases letters. Non-ASCII digits fail, but some Unicode letters normalize into accepted ASCII letters.

faq.question: Can this skill check old-format residence certificates or retrieve registry records?
faq.answer: No. Old-format residence certificates are unsupported, and the skill does not query company or personal registries.
